🌤 Leuchars Weather Climatology

NCAS St Andrews — Observed anomalies relative to the WMO 1991–2020 reference period

Station: Leuchars, Fife, Scotland (WMO 03171 / MIDAS 00235)
Coordinates: 56.377°N, 2.862°W, 10 m a.s.l.
Record: 1957–2024
Reference period: 1991–2020
Source: Met Office MIDAS Open, dataset-version-202507, qc-version-1

Figure 1 — Annual-mean anomalies: temperature, pressure, wind, humidity

Annual mean anomalies of air temperature (°C), mean sea-level pressure (hPa), wind speed (m s⁻¹) and relative humidity (%) relative to the 1991–2020 climatological mean. Bars: annual anomaly (darker = positive); black line: 11-year centred running mean; gold shading: reference period.

Figure 2 — Monthly temperature anomaly heatmap

Monthly mean air temperature anomaly (°C) for each year and calendar month. Blue = below the 1991–2020 mean; red = above. Dashed gold lines mark the reference period boundaries.

Figure 3 — Climatological diurnal cycle by season

Mean diurnal cycle of air temperature and wind speed over the 1991–2020 reference period, broken down by meteorological season (DJF, MAM, JJA, SON). Shading represents ±1 standard deviation across all years in the reference period. Times are UTC.

Figure 4 — Annual-mean anomalies: sunshine, cloud cover, visibility

Annual mean anomalies of sunshine duration (hr hr⁻¹), cloud cover (oktas) and visibility (m). Note: Campbell-Stokes sunshine data begin in 1980; derived sunshine and cloud cover span the full record where available.
